summary.ko: 돌다·돌리다 / 방향을 틀다 / (상태가) 되다 / 넘기다 / 차례 / 변화
summary.native: to move around a center; to change direction; to become; to move a page over; a time to act; a change

etymology.ko: 고대 영어 후기의 turnian과 고대 프랑스어 torner에서 왔고, 둘 다 라틴어 tornare('선반(旋盤)에 돌려 깎다, 둥글게 다듬다')에서 나왔다. 이 라틴어는 tornus('선반')에서, 다시 그리스어 tornos('선반, 원을 그리는 도구')에서 왔다. 중세 영어 turnen은 처음에 '축을 중심으로 돌다'를 뜻했다. 명사 '차례'는 14세기 초부터 쓰였는데, 여럿이 돌아가며 한다는 데서 나왔다. tour, tournament도 같은 뿌리다.
etymology.native: From late Old English turnian and Old French torner, both from Latin tornare, 'to turn on a lathe, to round off'. This came from tornus, 'lathe', from Greek tornos, 'lathe, tool for drawing circles'. Middle English turnen first meant 'rotate'. The noun sense 'a person's time to act, going round in order' dates from the early 14th century. Tour and tournament share the same root.

grammar.ko: 규칙 동사다: turn - turned - turned. '돌다'(자동사)와 '돌리다'(타동사)로 모두 쓴다.
grammar.native: Regular verb: turn, turned, turned. It is used both without an object (The wheel turns) and with one (Turn the key).

grammar.ko: 상태 변화는 turn + 형용사(turn red), turn into·to + 명사(turn into ice)로 쓴다. 나이는 turn + 숫자다(turn 30).
grammar.native: For a change of state, use turn + adjective (turn red) or turn into or to + noun (turn into ice). For age, use turn + number (turn 30).

grammar.ko: 방향은 전치사 없이 turn left, turn right라고 한다. 몸을 돌려 뒤를 보는 것은 turn around(영국 영어 turn round)다.
grammar.native: Directions usually need no preposition: turn left, turn right. To face the other way is turn around (British English: turn round).

grammar.ko: 명사 turn은 셀 수 있다(a turn, turns). 차례는 my turn, your turn처럼 소유격과 함께 쓰고, take turns (+ -ing)는 '번갈아 하다'다.
grammar.native: The noun is countable (a turn, turns). For someone's time to act, use my turn, your turn; take turns (+ -ing) means doing something one after another.

grammar.ko: 구동사가 많다: turn on·off(켜다·끄다), turn up·down(소리를 키우다·줄이다), turn down(거절하다), turn in(제출하다), turn out(~로 드러나다).
grammar.native: It forms many phrasal verbs: turn on and off, turn up and down (volume), turn down (refuse), turn in (hand in), turn out (prove to be).

meaning.native: to move around a central point, or to make something do this

usage.ko: 바퀴·손잡이·열쇠처럼 제자리에서 빙 도는 움직임에 쓴다. 손으로 돌리는 것(타동사)과 스스로 도는 것(자동사) 모두에 쓴다.
usage.native: Used for things such as wheels, handles, and keys that move in a circle. It can mean making something go round, or going round by itself.

examples.text: Turn the key to the right to open the door.
The wheels started to turn slowly.
The Earth turns once a day.

meaning.native: to change the direction you are moving or facing

usage.ko: 길을 가다 좌우로 꺾거나, 몸이나 고개를 다른 쪽으로 돌릴 때 쓴다. 길 안내에서 turn left, turn right가 가장 흔하다.
usage.native: Used for changing direction while moving, or turning your body or head to face another way. Turn left and turn right are very common in directions.

examples.text: Turn left at the next corner.
She turned around when I called her name.
Everyone turned to look at the door.
examples.ko: 모두 고개를 돌려 문 쪽을 보았다.

meaning.native: to become different, to change into something, or to reach an age

usage.ko: 색·날씨·상태가 바뀌거나 무엇이 다른 것으로 변할 때 쓴다. 뒤에 형용사, into·to + 명사, 나이를 나타내는 숫자가 온다.
usage.native: Used when a colour, the weather, or a situation changes, or something becomes something else. It is followed by an adjective, into or to + noun, or an age.

examples.text: The leaves turn red and yellow in autumn.
My son turns ten next month.
examples.ko: 우리 아들은 다음 달에 열 살이 된다.

examples.text: The rain turned to snow in the evening.
His small shop turned into a big company.
examples.ko: 그의 작은 가게는 큰 회사가 되었다.

meaning.native: to move a page so you can see the next one, or to move something so the other side faces up

usage.ko: 책장을 넘기거나 물건의 윗면과 아랫면을 뒤집을 때 쓴다. 뒤집을 때는 흔히 over를 붙인다(turn over).
usage.native: Used for moving the pages of a book or turning something upside down. For turning something upside down, over is often added (turn over).

examples.text: Please turn to page 25.
He turned the page and kept reading.
Turn the pancake over when bubbles appear.

meaning.native: the time when a person can or must do something, as people do it one after another

usage.ko: 여럿이 돌아가며 할 때 한 사람이 할 순서를 말한다. It's your turn(네 차례야)과 take turns(번갈아 하다)가 매우 흔하다.
usage.native: Used for one person's time to do something when people do it in order. It's your turn and take turns are very common.

examples.text: It's your turn to choose the restaurant.
Please wait your turn in line.
We took turns driving on the long trip.
examples.ko: 먼 여행길에 우리는 번갈아 가며 운전했다.

meaning.native: a change of direction when you are moving, or a place where a road goes in a new direction

usage.ko: 차나 사람이 방향을 트는 일, 또는 길이 꺾이는 곳을 말한다. make a turn, take a wrong turn처럼 쓴다.
usage.native: Used for a change of direction by a car or person, or a place where a road bends. Common phrases are make a turn and take a wrong turn.

examples.text: Make a left turn at the gas station.
I think we took a wrong turn somewhere.
examples.ko: 어디선가 길을 잘못 든 것 같아.

examples.text: U-turns are not allowed on this road.

meaning.native: a change in the way something is happening or developing

usage.ko: 상황이 갑자기 다른 쪽으로 흘러가는 것을 말한다. take a turn for the better(좋아지다), take a turn for the worse(나빠지다)가 흔하다.
usage.native: Used when a situation starts to go in a different direction. Take a turn for the better and take a turn for the worse are common.

collocations: take a turn for the better
take a turn for the worse

examples.text: The weather took a turn for the worse in the afternoon.
His health has taken a turn for the better.
The story takes a surprising turn at the end.

cautions.ko: '불을 켜다·끄다'에 open, close를 쓰지 않는다. 전등·텔레비전·에어컨은 turn on, turn off(또는 switch on, switch off)다.
cautions.native: Do not use open or close for lights and machines. Use turn on and turn off (or switch on and switch off).

cautions.ko: 한국어 '차례, 순서'를 order로 옮기면 어색하다. 내 차례는 my turn이고, order는 '배열된 순서'(in alphabetical order)다.
cautions.native: A person's time to act is a turn, not an order: It's my turn. Order is the way things are arranged (in alphabetical order).

cautions.ko: turn down은 '소리를 줄이다' 말고 '거절하다'라는 뜻으로도 자주 쓴다. She turned down the job offer.는 일자리 제의를 거절했다는 말이다.
cautions.native: Turn down means 'make quieter', but also 'refuse': She turned down the job offer.

cautions.ko: 나이를 말할 때는 turn이 자연스럽다. '다음 달에 서른이 된다'는 I turn 30 next month.(또는 I'll be 30)이다.
cautions.native: For reaching an age, turn is natural: I turn 30 next month, or I'll be 30 next month.

note.ko: 전등이나 기기를 켜고 끈다는 뜻이다. open과 close를 쓰지 않는다.
note.native: Means to switch a light or a device on and off. The verbs open and close are not used here.

patterns.example: Turn off the air conditioner before you go out.

note.ko: 저절로 어떤 색이나 상태로 바뀐다는 뜻이다. red, cold, sour처럼 상태를 말하는 말이 온다.
note.native: Means to change into a color or a state by itself, with words such as red, cold, or sour.

patterns.example: The leaves turn red in late October.

note.ko: 몇 살이 된다는 뜻이다. 생일을 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 말이다.
note.native: Means to reach a certain age, and it is the most natural way to speak about a birthday.

patterns.example: My father turns seventy next month.

note.ko: 네 차례라고 말하는 틀이다. 명사 turn은 순번을 뜻한다.
note.native: Says whose go it is. The noun turn means a place in a sequence.

patterns.example: It's your turn to wash the dishes tonight.

difference.ko: rotate는 축을 중심으로 빙 도는 것을 말하는 격식 있는 말이다. 일상적으로 돌린다는 말은 turn이다.
difference.native: Rotate is a formal word for spinning around an axis, while turn is the everyday word.

confusables.example: Turn the handle to rotate the whole wheel.

difference.ko: switch는 한쪽에서 다른 쪽으로 바꾼다는 뜻이다. 전등에 switch on도 쓰지만 turn on이 더 흔하다.
difference.native: Switch means changing from one thing to another. Switch on also works for a light, though turn on is more common.

confusables.example: Turn on the lamp, then switch to the other channel.

difference.ko: bend는 구부린다는 뜻이고, turn은 방향을 바꾼다는 뜻이다. 길이 꺾이는 곳을 a bend라고도 한다.
difference.native: Bend means to curve something, while turn means to change direction. A curve in a road can be called a bend.

confusables.example: Bend the wire, then turn left at the corner.
